notes:
Key account: building a real-time maritime operations assistant that needs strict latency and throughput guarantees across Pacific and US-East regions. Heavy use of chat + reranking for ETA predictions and route optimization. Team is cost-aware but will pay for predictable SLAs. Primary ask: reserved GPU pool planning across regions/AZs with failover headroom for peak season (Q3).

From discovery: engineering lead says 'we need p95 < 75ms for chat at 512 tokens and sustained 400 qps during peak bursts; reranking jobs can be batched but need 200 qps 99th percentile within 300ms'. Wants clear migration path from hosted to Dedicated then to Private VPC.

Security: must support SSO (SAML + Okta), KMS integration for model keys, and retention policies for logs. Data residency for EU customers is required (deploy dedicated pools in eu-west-1).

Commercial: prefers 12-month reserved commit with burst windows; wants SLA credits that scale with sustained misses not just incidents. Legal pushed back on unlimited fallback; asking for documented fallback policy and warm standby requirements.

POC notes: 2-week perf run completed 2025-01-30. Observed baseline: p50 28ms, p95 82ms on single-region small pool; multi-region routing added ~12-18ms depending on cross-region fallback. Need to size headroom for 2x baseline traffic for failover and 1.5x for seasonal peaks. SE suggests reserved pools: 40 A100-equivalent GPUs in us-east-1, 20 in us-west-2, 12 in eu-west-1, with cross-region warm standby.

AE remarks: pricing sensitivity around on-demand spillover. Customer requested bill protection when Redwood triggers failover due to capacity.

Actionable links: PoC perf sheet + cost model in Drive. Jira INF-2139 tracks kernel opt regressions; INF-2198 tracks region capacity confirmation with cloud provider.
